title: ReviewNarrative
description: Narrative layer an LLM produces on top of a merge request diff. The diff itself is NOT part of this payload: the tool already has it. The model only references files and hunks by their identity and attaches prose.

merge_request.description: Echoed back from the input so the narrative is self-contained. The model must not invent these values.

overview.description: The high-level page. Answers why before how; must be readable without looking at any code.

what.description: What the MR changes, in behavioural terms. 2-4 sentences. Name the public contract and say whether it moved.

why.description: The problem that motivated the change. 2-4 sentences. Ground it in something observable (a metric, a bug, a constraint), never in vague improvement.

risks.description: What could go wrong if the change is subtly incorrect. 1-3 sentences. Point at the step that carries the risk.

out_of_scope.description: Optional. Related work deliberately NOT done here, so the reviewer does not look for it.

steps.description: The review path. Ordered by the logic of the change (contract, then implementation, then wiring, then the delicate part, then config, then tests) — NOT by file path. A file may legitimately appear in more than one step if it was touched for more than one reason.

kind.description: Drives the step badge. Use "delicate" at most twice per MR — it is the reviewer's attention budget.

role.description: One short line: this step's job in the whole. Shown in the overview list.

intro.description: 2-3 sentences. What this step does and the decision behind it.

detail.description: Optional. Hidden in concise mode. Alternatives considered and why they were rejected.

files.description: Every file this step touches, in reading order.

path.description: Repository-relative path, exactly as in the diff.

why.description: Why THIS file changed the way it did. Explain the decision, not the diff — never restate lines the reviewer can read. 1-3 sentences.

watchpoints.description: Things the reviewer should actively check. Empty is a valid and common answer; do not pad. Each is one actionable sentence.

confidence.description: Optional. How sure the model is that this file is correct. "low" should always come with a watchpoint.

hunks.description: The hunks of this file that belong to this step. A file's hunks may be split across several steps: list here only those that serve THIS step's intent. Lines of code are not repeated — only their coordinates.

index.description: 0-based index of the hunk within this file's diff. Fast path for the renderer.

new_start.description: First line of the hunk in the file AFTER the change (the +N of the @@ header). Authoritative if index and coordinates disagree.

new_lines.description: Number of lines the hunk spans after the change. new_start + new_lines - 1 is the last line.

old_start.description: Optional. First line before the change (the -N of the @@ header). Set to 0 for an added file.

old_lines.description: Optional. Lines spanned before the change. 0 for a pure insertion.

focus_lines.description: Optional. The few post-change line numbers that actually carry the decision, inside [new_start, new_start + new_lines - 1]. Lets the reader jump to the 2 lines that matter in a 30-line hunk. Omit rather than list the whole hunk.

label.description: Optional short anchor shown above the code, e.g. "def verify".

note.description: Optional inline remark about this hunk specifically. Use rarely — the file-level why carries most of the meaning.
